newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids values flat; focus still on HSFO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids values flat; focus still on HSFO.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished Tuesday mostly flat versus Monday's values, with focus still on high sulphur grades, market sources said.
"It's basically flat from yesterday," said an East Coast trader, referring today's spot resid values despite weaker crude oil and natural gas prices.
In New York harbor and Gulf Coast, offers for high sulphur materials were up 25 cents a barrel from Monday to $17.50 amid tight availability and firm bunker demand.
Low sulphur grades in the both markets were thinly talked Tuesday because of lackluster end-user buying.
NYH physical one percent were again near $19.00 a barrel, with early October paper quote falling to $19.20-$19.50, off from Monday's $19.35-$19.65.
On Tuesday, NYMEX November crude futures settled down 24 cents at $24.14 and November Henry Hub natgas futures ended down 2.9 cents at $2.185 million British thermal units.
At the Gulf, one percent sulphur grade was unchanged at $17.50. A three percent Gulf deal was heard done at $17.50.
October New York City Gate gas was assessed little changed Tuesday at near the $2.20/mmBtu mark, compared with NYH one percent resid at $3.02/mmBtu equivalent.
